title: Integral derived tensor: lower bound and torsion cohomology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use the small etale derived category $D(T_{\Et})=D(\Ab(T_{\Et}))$ and its cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $A,B\in D(T_{\Et})$ and $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $\mathcal H^i(A)=0$ for $i<a$ and $\mathcal H^j(B)=0$ for $j<b$. For the ordinary derived tensor product over $\mathbf Z$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], one has
$$
\mathcal H^r(A\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}B)=0\qquad(r<a+b-1).
$$
If, in addition, every $\mathcal H^i(A)$ is a torsion abelian sheaf (as defined in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]), then every $\mathcal H^r(A\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}B)$ is a torsion abelian sheaf. No common integer annihilating these sheaves, no constructibility assumption, and no condition on the residue characteristics of $T$ is imposed.

proof.text: Flat integer sheaves are closed under subobjects. Check flatness at geometric stalks using lem-sfb-etale-flat-geometric-fibers. Stalks preserve monomorphisms, and a submodule of a flat module over the principal ideal domain ULift Z is torsion free and hence flat. This argument includes the zero sheaf and needs no residue-characteristic assumption.

Take a flat K-flat resolution P of A using the existing generic source theorem exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat (lem-sfb-abstract-kflat-resolution). Every complex of flat integer sheaves is K-flat: each upper good truncation is bounded above and flat, since its inclusion into the original complex is termwise mono, and the complex is their filtered colimit. Since P is exact in degree a-1, its opcycles in that degree embed in the next flat term. Thus its lower good truncation at a-1 is still flat and K-flat, is strictly zero below a-1, and represents A. Take a strict lower model L of B with bound b. The K-flat comparison identifies A tensor-derived B with Q(P-truncated tensor L), whose total tensor terms vanish below (a-1)+b. Transport the resulting cohomology bound across the comparison isomorphism.

For torsion cohomology of A, use the exact equivalence from sheaves of modules over ULift Z to abelian sheaves, induced by integer coefficient restriction and the Z-module/abelian-group equivalence. The derived equivalence commutes with homology. Apply lem-trf-torsion-sheaf-complex-representative to obtain a complex L with torsion terms representing the underlying abelian derived object, and transport L back by the inverse equivalence. Its terms are torsion integer sheaves and Q(L) is isomorphic to A. No object is defined by choosing an arbitrary witness: all witnesses are eliminated only inside this theorem proof.

Resolve B by a flat K-flat complex P. The derived tensor is represented by L tensor P. A tensor product of a torsion module with an arbitrary module is torsion, because each pure tensor is the image of a torsion element under the additive map x maps to x tensor y, and finite sums of torsion elements are torsion. Strong monoidality of the geometric stalk functor transfers this to sheaf tensors. Torsion abelian groups are closed under arbitrary colimits: each colimit injection factors through the torsion subgroup of the colimit, yielding a retraction of its inclusion by the universal property, hence that subgroup is the whole group. Stalks preserve the small coproducts forming each total tensor term, so every term of L tensor P is a torsion sheaf. Its cycles are a subobject of its terms and its homology is a quotient of the cycles, so its homology is torsion. Transport along the derived tensor and homology comparison isomorphisms and use the local/stalkwise torsion criterion.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Proved the integral lower bound and torsion closure on geometric stalks using the bounded integral Kunneth exact sequence, then extended the calculation by two termwise truncation colimits using an existing module derived-tensor theorem. The single new node is bounded Kunneth for ordinary abelian groups, not a clause of the sheaf conclusion. All citations checked against statements. No Lean or builds. Source inequalities in Stacks 0F0F are already corrected in the item; the generic stronger tensor-connectivity node is false and is not used. Second reading replaces the off-unit symmetry descent citation by the existing symmetry theorem of this unit and writes the two colimit comparisons and their transition compatibility explicitly.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the preliminary boundedness and torsion input of lem-kun-0f0f, proof before the proper base-change reduction (Stacks 0F0F). Keeps the unit named 0F0F route. The unit has no proof steps of its own. New bounded Kunneth supplies the integral global-dimension-one calculation; truncation colimits give the bounded-below case.

tool_uses.why: The trivial-Galois field-site equivalence identifies the small etale topos of a geometric point with abelian groups; no statement of this unit supplies this generic field-site fact.
A generic module derived-tensor/cohomology continuity theorem permits two bounded truncation colimits; this unit has no corresponding ordinary-module continuity statement.
The ordinary Tor symmetry permits computing Tor1 against a torsion group in the unresolved factor; no node of this unit gives that module homology theorem.
The generic equivalence between local annihilation and torsion geometric stalks converts the hypothesis and conclusion; the unit does not prove this sheaf criterion.
